top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, a mature and independently reproduced result: lattice light shifts, collisions and blackbody shifts are quantitatively controlled, independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level, and millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and many-body effects in the lattice have been measured. The Katori (architecture, early demonstrations) and Ye (accuracy and stability) split is a defensible two-name allocation, and the narrow citation on neutral atoms at the magic wavelength with many-atom interrogation avoids reading as a general metrology prize or a repeat of 2005 and 2012. Reservations about priority (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley) and about the prospective fundamental payoffs do not outweigh this, and no award is the weaker option when a verified, well-scoped achievement is available.
